title: Maximum Runtime With Swappable APIs
statement:
A team has `N` APIs and wants to run `M` applications at the same time, where `M ≤ N`. API `i` can run for a total of `runtime[i]` minutes. Every application needs exactly one API running for it at every moment.

Initially each application is given one API. At any moment a running API may be stopped and later restarted any number of times (an API's total running time across all its starts is limited to `runtime[i]`). An application may be moved from one API to another, including an API that another application was using before. Stopping, starting and swapping cost no time, and an API can serve at most one application at a time.

Find the **maximum whole number of minutes** `T` such that all `M` applications can keep running simultaneously for `T` minutes.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer `N`, the number of APIs.
The second line contains `N` space-separated integers: `runtime[0] ... runtime[N-1]`.
The third line contains an integer `M`, the number of applications.
output_format: Print a single integer: the maximum number of minutes all `M` applications can run simultaneously.

examples.explanation: The three APIs offer 9 minutes in total, so two applications get at most 4 minutes each (8 in total), and 5 each would need 10. Four is reachable by swapping: in minutes 1 to 4 application A uses APIs 0, 0, 2, 2 and application B uses APIs 1, 1, 0, 1. No API runs more than 3 minutes.
The big API can serve only one application at a time. One application uses it, the other must live off the two 1-minute APIs, which give only 2 minutes in total.
20 minutes of API time shared by 3 applications gives at most 6 minutes each (18 minutes used), and every API is short enough (5 < 6) to be shared freely.

hints: If all M applications run for T minutes, an API can contribute at most min(runtime[i], T) minutes, because it cannot serve two applications at once.
T is feasible exactly when the sum of min(runtime[i], T) over all APIs is at least M * T. Feasibility is monotone in T, so binary search works.

Alternatively sort the APIs. An API longer than (remaining total) / (remaining applications) can only be dedicated to one application, so remove it together with one application and repeat; the answer is then total // applications.
reference:
import sys


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    a = sorted(int(v) for v in data[1:1 + n])
    m = int(data[1 + n])
    total = sum(a)
    i = n - 1
    while a[i] * m > total:
        total -= a[i]
        m -= 1
        i -= 1
    print(total // m)


main()

import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
rem = [int(v) for v in data[1:1 + n]]
m = int(data[1 + n])
minutes = 0
while True:
    rem.sort(reverse=True)
    if rem[m - 1] < 1:
        break
    for i in range(m):
        rem[i] -= 1
    minutes += 1
print(minutes)
